words.definition: A state of hardship, misfortune, or difficulty.
words.example: She showed great strength and resilience in the face of adversity.

words.definition: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a way that is based on practical rather than theoretical considerations.
words.example: A pragmatic approach to study scheduling ensures you cover all subjects before the exam.

words.definition: To make less severe, serious, or painful.
words.example: Reviewing daily flashcards helps mitigate the stress of exam preparation.

words.definition: Open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous, uncertain, or questionable.
words.example: The politician gave an equivocal answer when asked about the proposed tax reforms.

words.definition: Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.
words.example: A meticulous review of the clerical questions can save you from spelling mistakes.

words.definition: Well-meaning and kindly; serving a charitable rather than a profit-making purpose.
words.example: The benevolent supervisor offered to mentor the new civil service interns.

words.definition: Having knowledge or being aware of something.
words.example: Reviewees must be cognizant of the rules governing the examination rooms.

words.definition: Sharpness or severity; intellectual alertness or penetration.
words.example: Her mathematical acuteness helped her solve the complex numerical series instantly.

words.definition: Careful and persistent work or effort.
words.example: Your diligence in studying will pay off on the day of the Civil Service Exam.
